svg.text: BAS Commissioning — Verify the Inputs Before You Trust the Control Logic
Points verification — the first BAS Cx step
Confirm every sensor reads reality and
every actuator command moves the
CORRECT physical device.
AHU-1's economizer damper command
must move AHU-1's damper, not AHU-2's.
Sensor calibration — the silent failure
A 5°F sensor offset triggers NO alarm —
it just makes the wrong decision, all day,
every day, silently.
Verify against calibrated reference instruments
Worked example — a +5°F SAT sensor offset
Controller thinks supply air is 5°F warmer than it actually is → calls for more cooling to reach setpoint
→ delivers overcooled air, wastes energy, and never trips an alarm on its own.
Also common: CO2 drift, un-zeroed static pressure sensors, RH sensors degraded by liquid water exposure.
Sequence of operation (SOO) verification — a desk review, not a field test
Compare the programmed sequence (controls contractor's documentation) against the specified
sequence in the mechanical spec — before any field time is spent.
Discrepancies found here cost nothing but reading time; the same gap found in the field costs a failed test.
